prompt: shrink this codebase — it's gotten really bloated
expected_output: Standard mode selects 2-3 relevant bloat roles from pre-pass evidence, baseline LOC is measured, tests run before changes, findings are applied in safe batches, and the final report shows lines removed with before/after tests.
expectations: Skill triggers on 'shrink this codebase' phrasing
Establishes baseline LOC before any changes
Runs tests before making changes
Spawns only 2-3 relevant roles in standard mode; all four are reserved for thorough mode
Writes findings JSON files to the resolved WORKSPACE
Writes STAGED_CHANGES.md before applying any edits
Runs tests after applying changes
Reverts changes that cause test failures
Never runs git commit
Prints final report with LOC before and after

prompt: remove all the dead code from this repo and make it smaller
expected_output: Skill triggers (dead code removal + make smaller = shrinkray scope). The Dead Code and Ghost File roles run because both are directly relevant, report confidence, and changes are verified.
expectations: Skill triggers on 'remove dead code' combined with size reduction intent
Dead Code Hunter subagent specifically searches for unreachable code
Ghost File Hunter searches for unreferenced files
Each change is logged with category and estimated LOC saved
Tests pass after all changes
Final report breaks down lines removed by category

expected_output: Explicit skill invocation. Standard pipeline executes setup, 2-3 evidence-selected bloat roles, triage, apply, verify, and convergence checks.
expectations: Skill triggers on explicit 'run shrinkray' command
Detects test runner automatically
Measures baseline LOC
Spawns only evidence-selected roles in standard mode
Applies changes with per-change syntax checks
Runs full test suite after changes
Stops when converged or 5 iterations elapsed

prompt: can you review this code and find bugs?
expected_output: Skill does NOT trigger. Bug finding without size reduction is code-smellz territory or a simple review. Shrinkray should be skipped.
expectations: Skill does NOT trigger on pure bug-finding requests
Claude answers the review request directly or suggests code-smellz instead

prompt: minify my JavaScript bundle for production
expected_output: Skill does NOT trigger. JS bundle minification (webpack/esbuild) is a build tool concern, not a source code restructuring task.
expectations: Skill does NOT trigger on JS/CSS bundle minification requests
Claude suggests using the appropriate build tool instead

prompt: Trim one verbose helper function in helpers.py — it's the only obvious bloat in the file.
expected_output: Takes the lite tier: reviews that one function directly — no subagents spawned. A single-function verbosity trim meets none of the Hard Spawn Gate criteria, so the four-agent crew is not spawned at all.
expectations: States the mode line (mode: lite ...; budget: 0) before editing
Takes the lite tier — spawns NO subagents to trim a single function (meets no Hard Spawn Gate criterion)
Shortens the helper without changing behavior

prompt: shrink this codebase --quick — fast pass, just grab the obvious bloat.
expected_output: The explicit --quick flag pins the lite tier regardless of codebase size: runs the dead-code pre-pass, applies clear-cut findings directly (no four-agent crew), one pass. Still measures LOC, runs available tests, reverts anything that breaks, and emits a DONE: line.
expectations: States the mode line (mode: lite (--quick); budget: 0) before cleanup
The --quick flag is honored — lite tier pinned by the explicit flag, not by task-size auto-detection
Does NOT spawn the four-agent crew in parallel (direct review only)
Runs scripts/deadcode_scan.py as a pre-pass and consults its findings
Still measures baseline LOC and runs tests if available
Never runs git commit
Emits a DONE: signal with LOC removed

prompt: shrink this repo, it's gotten bloated over the years
expected_output: Standard mode runs the dead-code pre-pass (deadcode_scan.py) before any agent dispatch. Dead Code Hunter and Ghost File Hunter consume the pre-pass findings and verify-and-apply rather than discover from scratch. Tool-certified findings get confidence=high and source_tool set; LLM-discovered ones get source_tool=null.
expectations: Runs scripts/deadcode_scan.py as Phase 0.5 and writes deadcode_scan.json to the workspace
Threads the deadcode_scan.json path to Dead Code Hunter as {{deadcode_scan_path}}
Dead Code Hunter prompt is verify-and-apply: each finding references a tool-flagged candidate with grep verification, not a guess from reading
Findings with tool certification carry source_tool (e.g. vulture, knip, tsc); LLM-only findings carry source_tool=null
Type-check or syntax gate runs after each apply (Phase 4)
Second-minimizer pass (Phase 3.3) re-runs deadcode_scan.py on affected files after successful applies
Never runs git commit
Emits DONE: with LOC removed

prompt: find bugs and security issues in this codebase
expected_output: Skill does NOT trigger. Bug/security review is code-smellz territory, not size reduction. Shrinkray should be skipped.
expectations: Skill does NOT trigger on bug/security review requests
Claude answers directly or suggests code-smellz instead

prompt: shrink this codebase --thorough — we have a lot of structural debt: wrappers around stdlib, single-implementor interfaces, stable feature flags nobody will flip back, near-duplicate modules.
expected_output: Thorough mode runs both pre-pass scripts (deadcode_scan.py + dependency_index.py), dispatches the four primary roles AND the five structural roles with propose-then-implement decomposition. The Indirection Inliner and Module Merger consume dependency_index.json; their findings cite index entries (single_caller_symbols, single_importer_files). Structural role findings went through a proposal file before patches were written.
expectations: States mode: thorough; budget: 5 (or equivalent) before dispatch
Runs both pre-pass scripts: scripts/deadcode_scan.py and scripts/dependency_index.py
Dispatches all five structural roles (Stdlib Replacer, Indirection Inliner, Table-Drive Converter, Flag Pruner, Module Merger) in addition to primary roles
Indirection Inliner findings cite dependency_index.json's single_caller_symbols or single_implementor_interfaces
Module Merger findings cite dependency_index.json's single_importer_files
Structural roles ran a proposal pass first; patches came only after orchestrator selection (no patches for negative-net-savings candidates)
Type-check / syntax gate runs after each apply
Second-minimizer pass re-runs deadcode_scan.py on affected files
Never runs git commit
Emits DONE: with LOC removed

prompt: shrink the codebase, but the structural roles keep introducing risky changes that don't fit --standard.
expected_output: Standard mode dispatches only primary roles (Dead Code Hunter, Ghost File Hunter, Code Consolidator, Verbosity Reducer) and skips the five structural roles. Structural roles are reserved for --thorough. Skill should still run both pre-pass scripts in standard mode (the dependency_index is used by Code Consolidator too).
expectations: States mode: standard; budget: 3 (or equivalent)
Runs both pre-pass scripts in standard mode
Does NOT dispatch Stdlib Replacer, Indirection Inliner, Table-Drive Converter, Flag Pruner, or Module Merger in standard mode
Code Consolidator consumes dependency_index.json even in standard mode
No propose-then-implement decomposition runs in standard mode (Phase 1.5 is structural-roles-only)
